title.label: AMAZING for students, but there is only one issue

content.label: I’m a virtual high school student (early high school), I have always had a hard time focusing when completing tasks that require intensive focus, like typing an essay, making a presentation, studying, taking notes, completing a review, etc. Portal has helped me a lot, however, after 7 days passed i realized just how limited my options are, especially for HD portals, as there’s only three available without a subscription currently. Unfortunately, not many high school students out there are able to pay $70/year for a Portal premium subscription, or pay $300 for a lifetime subscription. Although an exclusive option for students to get Portal for a lower price, a wider range of free portals would help people like me out a ton. I’m already paying for a lot of other things on my own, and while I understand how important the subscriptions and their profit is, students like me who really benefit off of portal are not in the position to pay for one. All of that aside, amazing app! Would definitely recommend to anyone looking for an app to help clear distractions off their mind.

title.label: Not bad - I just need a little more to justify it.

content.label:
Pros: 
-This is great for people who don’t like it completely quiet or use it to sleep and work. 
- the interfaces are gorgeous and there is good variety. All Beaches, mountains, woods, greenery, and 1 fire. 
- I love that I can use it on most of the Apple ecosystem - more on that below.
-there’s a built in timer and alarm which is great for workers
- I loved that I could play the interfaces in the background while moving on to another app like my kindle app or shopping apps.
-my family liked having access to it on their devices too 

Cons:
- there are some people who like a “soft city” setting which is pretty common in the ambient world. A little surprised that one is not included for this app. 
-a majority of the interfaces are for places like Switzerland and Iceland which is great, but I was hoping they’d add a few more from different places throughout the year I had it - like more from Hawaii, Africa, Canada, South America, etc…and of course, a city one or something of that nature.
-some of the interfaces move more beautifully than others. As in, some of the interfaces don’t seem to move at all. They are standstills with the ambient noise in the background. Obviously, I enjoy the ones that I can see moving for an immersive feel.
-I see that there’s information about the price being different depending on which geographical app store you are using. However, I bought the annual subscription last year for $49.99 from my I-Phone. And it says it’s $69.99 now from my IPad. I’m seeing two different prices from two different devices. I don’t really like that…So you could potentially be charged differently depending on the device you use. I have not moved locations or have any different settings on my devices that could cause that. So look at the pricing from different devices if you consider purchasing the subscription, because that is strange. I would think it would be the same across all platforms if my location and settings haven’t changed….
-nevertheless, let’s say the “true” new price is now $70 for someone in my location for the year a - I just don’t see how it would be worth it at this time. In the past year, nothing has changed on the app for users except the inclusion of one new portal. I saw the developers response to someone bringing up the subscription model, but with the price increase based on your device and geography, I definitely think there could be more interfaces dropped throughout the year to justify a price increase too. Again, for the year I had it, I can only think of one new interface released and I believe it was for an Iceland volcano - which we have quite a few of already. 
-My biggest ire is that given this work on your phone computer or iPad, I really wish or hope to see them develop a Portal app for Apple TV. All my family and friends play ambience on their TVs. Even some teachers I know use it on their school TVs, but we all have to rely on ambience interfaces from YouTube because there is not a robust app that can offer these interfaces otherwise through a TV.  It would be amazing to see portal migrate to that. Then I think that lifetime membership of $299.99 would be well worth it regardless of if they update with yearly portals or not! I play ambience on my Tele daily but something like that would mean I never have to use YouTube again. For now, I just can’t really justify the subscription or price increase until I see what else they do with the app. 

Side note: while I understand that practically every business is about that subscription life to essentially “help them grow”, you do not have to pay for a sub to enjoy this app. There’s 6 free ones available unless they decide to make them all subscribe to play and those particular portals are actually really good ones.

title.label: Love it but still hope it could be better

content.label:
I absolutely love this App. I've always wanted to find excellent dynamic wallpapers of nature in 4K+ resolution for my MAC system, but the results were generally mediocre until I discovered Portal. I immediately became a subscriber and now use Portal as a startup application and dynamic wallpaper on all my Mac computers. Choosing my favorite Portal scene has become a habit right after starting up my computer.

However, I think there are two areas where Portal could improve for me personally:

1. The price-to-content ratio. Yes, I think the price is a bit high. I understand the importance of subscription fees, especially for sustaining a small development team's operations. However, to be honest, I feel the number of available Portals is too limited relative to the subscription cost. While all the videos are premium quality, for a user like me who subscribes annually and habitually sets Portal as wallpaper immediately after startup every day, the current quantity and update frequency are indeed insufficient. I hope the update frequency could be increased.

2. The subscription model. For users who want to use Portal long-term, I wish there was a lifetime subscription option with an appropriate price point that motivates people to purchase. I haven't found this option on Mac OS.

Overall, I love Portal and hope it continues to improve, providing high-quality videos and experiences to users more frequently and in greater numbers.

Portal has been a game-changer for my focus and productivity, especially as a high school student juggling a busy schedule. Not only is the app fantastic for creating a calm and immersive work environment, but the customer support is also next level! Stu from the team went out of his way to make sure I had the best experience, even offering a free year of premium. Highly recommend Portal for anyone looking to improve their focus, and the support team is always there if you need them. Thank you, Portal!

title.label: Amazing App, surpassed only by the quality of their service

content.label:
I’ve been using Portal for about 4-5 years now and can’t imagine falling to sleep without the likes of Pacific Waves, Neist Point Lighthouse, Radovna Hut Rain & Amazon Thunderstorm (to name a few).

After upgrading to the iPhone 16 Pro yesterday, I noticed that I was unable to download most of my favorite portals.  I waited until Saturday morning to email Portal support and to my surprise received a prompt reply from Stu.  After a few questions, Stu was able to resolve the issue same day, outstanding service for a weekend, totally blew me away I’d even heard back, let alone have the issue resolved.

While the audio of Portal has always impressed, it’s the attention to excellent customer service that is over the top for me.  Thank you Stu and the whole Portal team for what you do, really appreciate you guys and sleep like a baby listening to your app!

There’s a few features that would really help:

1. Pausing turns off the video entirely. It would be nice if it just paused the video and served as a static wallpaper at times that I want to save on battery.
2. The ability to list every scene on one screen. I appreciate breaking things up based off activity ("Focus", "Create", "Escape"), but you soon realize that things are repeating or that the lists aren’t very long. 
3. Favorite icon is heart to distinguish toggle states. Since the settings icon is a filled in gear, seeing a filled in heart of the same color gray is confusing. There should be either a suble color *or* a darker stroke around heart icon.
4. Option-clicking the taskbar icon should show a menu that let’s me quickly quit the application. Instead it’s the same screen and I have to jump into the settings to do so.
5. Feedback screen that I’m writing in should support scrolling (might be an Apple bug and not developer’s fault)
